newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Offset purchases of Israeli products up 18 percent.
newsitem.headline: Offset purchases of Israeli products up 18 percent.

text.p: Offset purchasing of Israeli products by foreign companies increased 18 percent in 1996 to $1.07 billion, the Industry and Trade Ministry said on Sunday.

A spokesman said Israel had offset purchasing agreements with more than 400 foreign companies including McDonnel Douglas Corp, IBM, Digital, General Electric and Lockheed Martin. Roughly the same number of Israeli companies made sales through offset agreements, the ministry said.
Most agreements were in aviation, electronic and electrical appliances, steel and computers.
During 1996, the ministry added, it had signed new offset agreements with 30 other companies, among them Volvo, GEC Alstrom Goodyear, and Fiat.

The ministry assists Israeli companies in winning contracts in the framework of offset agreements, under which the government conditions its procurements on the seller's agreeing to buy Israeli products.
